# Aegis

> Aegis is a Windows-first open-source desktop app for local AI-agent oversight: process/file/TCP monitoring, local security review, resource/token accounting, audit reports and explicit action policies/MCP gateways. macOS/Linux support is experimental.

Historical source checkpoint: 18 October 2026, merged master 96b63b165ac932e9615815f93c587765e6bde1b8 (PR #975). The published Windows 0.19.2-beta installer is dated 6 October; later source changes need a later installer release.

Current Windows x64 source packages include experimental Kernel-File reads in Events. Capture stays off on startup and requires an explicit local folder, Start and manual UAC consent; Stop, monitoring pause, suspend or quit request cleanup. Paths remain candidates, and potential path-rule risk does not inspect contents or update risk scoring, audit, baselines or sequences. Historical source-bound qualification includes the #975 warmup read, #976 diagnostic first/persistent reads and ordinary idle first reads after 65, 70 and 85 seconds on source 5249c10a. These receipts do not qualify changed protocol-10/package/harness inputs or a Windows restart; #974 reboot recovery remains pending. See [ordinary file reads](https://github.com/antropos17/Aegis/blob/master/docs/development/ordinary-file-reads.md) and [Windows recovery admission](https://github.com/antropos17/Aegis/blob/master/docs/roadmap/windows-recovery-admission.md).

Current source also provides opt-in exact-action execution policies and explicitly configured MCP action routes. Default monitoring does not intercept commands or isolate agents. A separate opt-in Windows Job route can bound the lifetime of ordinary descendants of one selected action after confirmed cleanup; it does not restrict file or network access. The separate AppContainer confirmation CLI verifies a zero-capability Windows token and Job for one bounded action in a new retained workspace. Installed builds contain only the features at their release tag.

Experimental administrative Hyper-V APIs can create a private VM, hydrate its original disk from a trusted Windows VHDX and run one bounded package as a fresh ordinary guest user. Actual boot, an enforced 512 MiB allocation quota, Job descendant closure, native Off and owned VM removal passed hosted qualification on source 5113e3b5d8473d105776e92d4830d6824d3f4c5d. Ordinary installed-caller launch, authenticated runtime communication, cancellation/owner-loss supervision and result review remain incomplete; independent enforcement A1-A4 acceptance remains open and launchAllowed=false. Unknown VMMS work has no recovery/restart API.

## Key Features

- Process monitoring with 112 known AI agents (265 process-name signatures) and parent-child tree resolution
- File system watching for sensitive directories (.ssh, .aws, .gnupg, .env, cloud configs)
- Network activity logging with per-agent PID tracking and reverse DNS
- Passive running WSL distribution-name inventory and local Docker/Linux-native Podman container candidates, with bounded configuration observations and explicit freshness; no guest process execution or independently verified internal agent identity
- Behavioral analysis with 73 detection rules across 8 categories
- Trust scoring with grades A+ through F using time-decay algorithms
- Local LLM detection (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, llama.cpp)
- Claude Code measured usage from matching local session data with durable deduplication, incomplete-coverage flags and estimated costs; other agents can show estimates
- Export to JSON, CSV, HTML reports and ZIP archives
- YAML rulesets with JSON Schema validation; edits to existing files hot-reload in unpacked runs
- Explicit policy-controlled direct child execution, with optional fresh terminal confirmation for one launch attempt
- Selected-action MCP catalogs of up to eight fixed argument-free action tools, with revision binding and optional terminal review per call
- Nonexecuting route/catalog configuration checks and read-only current-MCP-connection counters; neither grants execution permission nor proves outside-route coverage
- Node-only MCP client configuration generation for selected-action, catalog or relay routes; emits an `mcpServers.aegis` entry for explicit client loading, without reading selected files or installing settings
- Observatory Action control workspace: main-owned native file selection and nonexecuting route/catalog checks; captured results do not establish a connected agent or verified blocking
- Opt-in --observe endpoint for selected/catalog MCP owners: separate read-only desktop observation, bounded counters, self-reported client label/version and sticky coverage loss; no independently verified provider identity or blocking
- Local security workspace: selected project/profile static reviews, bounded inventory, saved snapshot comparison and offline report import, with explicit coverage limits
- Guided Observatory navigation with distinct local SVG icons, task search, result-first review screens and optional technical details; English and Brazilian Portuguese
- Explicit validating MCP gateways for selected stdio, loopback HTTP and pinned HTTPS servers, with accepted catalogs, finite schema validation and exact grants
- Optional expiring persistent MCP grants with route/credential/launch binding and known-secret checks for explicitly supplied values and listed encodings
- One exact selected-file deletion operation with mandatory terminal review, also exposed by a dedicated argument-free terminal MCP tool
- Administrative protected VM/image creation, original-disk hydration, identity-bound native lifecycle and one standard-user guest agent operation: no NICs, private desktop, explicit environment, 512 MiB allocation quota, 32-process Job, 512 MiB per-process/aggregate Job memory and 120-second maximum runtime

Local monitoring has no telemetry; endpoint naming uses DNS queries. Optional AI analysis sends activity metadata to Anthropic on request; update actions contact GitHub. AEGIS does not automatically enforce OS-level restrictions.

Direct and Job-only execution retain caller file/network privileges. The explicit AppContainer confirmation route adds OS access checks, zero capabilities and Job cleanup, with separate receipts for isolation, retained workspace and temporary-profile cleanup. Installed agents and ordinary launches do not enter it automatically. Private action previews can expose secrets in terminal scrollback; a TTY does not authenticate human presence. No client settings are changed automatically.

Generated client configuration intentionally includes local executable and selected-file paths. Keep it private; generation does not verify those files or a client's compatibility.

MCP gateways cover their explicitly configured traffic only. Known-secret checks are not general DLP; general OAuth, recipient/scope enforcement and arbitrary content-channel validation remain incomplete. Guest images, administrators and privileged guest services remain trust inputs; the allocation quota does not constrain writes charged to other principals. A hosted lab PASS does not establish a protected provider or production session.

## Technical Details

- **Stack**: Electron, Svelte 5, Vite; CommonJS JavaScript in main, TypeScript in the renderer and shared types. Exact versions: package.json
- **Tests**: Vitest; run `npm test` for current pass/skip and file counts
- **License**: MIT
- **Version**: 0.21.0-beta <!-- x-release-please-version -->
- **Platform**: Windows primary; macOS/Linux experimental
